findings.title: Config construction duplicated between fixture and _make_config helper
findings.description: In tests/test_orchestrator.py, the Config dataclass is constructed in two nearly-identical places: the config pytest fixture and the _make_config helper function. Both set the same fields with the same defaults. Any future field addition to Config must be updated in two places.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the config pytest fixture and replace it with a call to _make_config(tmp_path), or promote _make_config to the fixture with an optional max_articles parameter.

findings.title: Default values for Config fields duplicated in dataclass and load_config
findings.description: max_fetch_attempts=10 and max_articles_per_run=30 are hardcoded both as Config dataclass field defaults and as the fallback literals in data.get() inside load_config. The two sets must stay in sync manually.
findings.suggestedFix: Define defaults as module-level constants (e.g. _DEFAULT_MAX_FETCH_ATTEMPTS = 10) and reference them in both the dataclass field default and the data.get() call.

findings.title: Duplicate dict key lookup in load_config
findings.description: data["pinboard_feed_url"] was accessed twice in load_config: once assigned to url for validation and once again inside the Config() constructor, despite url already holding the validated value.
findings.suggestedFix: Use pinboard_feed_url=url in the Config() constructor instead of data["pinboard_feed_url"].

findings.title: _process_article too long (67 lines, two distinct concerns)
findings.description: _process_article mixed fetch+cache logic with extract+status-update logic in 67 lines, making each concern harder to read and test in isolation.
findings.suggestedFix: Extract _fetch_raw_html(url, config, entry, status_data, now_iso) to handle cache lookup, fetch, failure tracking, and status writing. _process_article delegates to it and handles extraction separately.
findings.patternReference: Private helper functions with underscore prefix

findings.title: store.write_status called redundantly at end of run_pipeline
findings.description: _process_article writes status atomically after each article. The unconditional store.write_status at the end of run_pipeline was always redundant with the last in-loop write when at least one article was processed.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the final store.write_status call in run_pipeline. Update test_status_written_after_each_article to assert >= 2 (1 write per article for 2 articles).

findings.title: status_data.get('articles', {}) repeated inline
findings.description: The same dict access pattern appears in both filter_articles and _filter_archive in orchestrator.py. Extractable to a one-liner private helper.
findings.patternReference: Private helper functions with underscore prefix

findings.title: Feed item dict structure is implicit across fetcher and test helper
findings.description: The _item test helper hard-codes {url, title, timestamp} without a shared schema. Silently diverges if fetcher renames a key.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce a FeedItem TypedDict or dataclass in courier/fetcher.py and use it in the test helper.

findings.title: Redundant if/else for config_path in load_config
findings.description: The 4-line if/else block was collapsible to a single ternary expression without loss of clarity.
findings.suggestedFix: config_path = Path(path) if path is not None else Path("config.toml")

findings.title: Deep .get() chain after _process_article re-navigates a guaranteed entry
findings.description: status_data.get("articles",{}).get(url,{}).get("status","") re-navigated three levels after _process_article guaranteed the entry exists via setdefault.

findings.title: Late import in test_orchestrator.py
findings.description: from courier.config import load_config appeared after test functions instead of at the top of the file with other imports.
findings.suggestedFix: Move the import to the top-level import block.

findings.title: test_article_cap_enforced constructs Config inline instead of using _make_config
findings.description: The only test that ignored the shared _make_config helper, causing a redundant inline Config construction with the same fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the inline Config(...) with _make_config(tmp_path, max_articles=2).

findings.title: Magic string "2" in cap-message assertion is fragile
findings.description: assert "2" in caplog.text could match any log line containing the digit 2, not necessarily the exclusion count message.
findings.suggestedFix: Assert on assert "2 articles excluded" in caplog.text to tie the assertion to the actual log message format.

findings.title: _now_iso() called up to 3 times per article
findings.description: Each call creates a fresh datetime.now(timezone.utc). A single capture at the start of _process_article is consistent and avoids repeated calls.
findings.suggestedFix: Capture now_iso = _now_iso() once at the top of _process_article and pass it to _fetch_raw_html and the extraction failure branch.

patternsPreserved.description: Each module independently declares logger = logging.getLogger(__name__). Repeated per-module but documented as the module-level logger pattern.
Each module starts with its own import block rather than a shared imports shim, following one-responsibility-per-module.
Exception handling in __main__.py catches FileNotFoundError, KeyError, and ValueError separately with distinct user-facing messages. Not copy-paste duplication.
patternsPreserved.patternName: Raise standard exceptions for configuration errors

patternsPreserved.description: Article dataclass is defined once in compiler.py and imported elsewhere. No duplication.
Test isolation via plain assert statements and inline data construction follows documented testing pattern.
Config and Article are PascalCase dataclasses as the primary structured data containers.
Configuration errors in load_config raise FileNotFoundError, KeyError, and ValueError as prescribed.
patternsPreserved.patternName: Raise standard exceptions for configuration errors

patternsPreserved.description: Internal helpers _fetch_and_parse_feed, _filter_archive, _parse_timestamp, _process_article, _fetch_raw_html, _log_summary, _now_iso all use a leading underscore.
patternsPreserved.patternName: Private helper functions with underscore prefix

patternsPreserved.description: filter_articles is a public function in orchestrator.py, exported and tested directly.
_env and _template constants in compiler.py are module-level, defined before any function definitions.
Configuration is loaded from TOML and mapped to a typed Config dataclass.
The | safe filter in document.xhtml is intentional with an inline trust-boundary comment.
Tests use plain assert statements with inline data construction per documented testing pattern.
Jinja2 Environment and template constructed once at module import as _env and _template constants.
filter_articles uses frozenset for _SKIP_STATUSES and _ARCHIVE_SKIP_STATUSES, giving O(1) membership tests.
Filesystem-based SHA-256 URL hashing for the cache avoids redundant HTTP fetches. Correctly applied via read_cached_html before fetch_article.
patternsPreserved.patternName: Caching strategy: Filesystem-based with SHA-256 URL hashing

patternsPreserved.description: store.write_status is called after every individual article for crash-safety. This is tested in test_status_written_after_each_article.
Template iterates articles twice (TOC and body). Inherent to XHTML output format; not a performance concern.
